payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_qualify.py::test_a_layer_whose_record_cannot_be_used_keeps_the_packaged_heads_check stayed green with the spec's wrong version "The record is bound by any REVIEW line naming its hash, so a later task's record is read as this task's." applied to saffron/qualify.py as an edit. The claim was "A layer with in-cell concerns whose record cannot be used keeps the drop from the packaged head to the graded head as before. It calls `note` once, with `reviewed_diff`, `False`, and `<spec id>: <cause>, so its in-cell concerns are checked from the packaged head`. The witness drives six causes on the stacked layer, each in its own tree, while the unstacked layer's record stays bound. The causes are `no reviewed-diff.json`, and `reviewed-diff.json is unreadable` for a truncated file. They go on with `its sha256 does not match its diff` and `no REVIEW line binds it to this task`. The last two are `the mirror lacks its tree base <sha>` and `its diff does not apply to <sha>`. In the other task's case, a `RecordAppend` under the layer's own key ends the log, as `saffron reconcile` writes one long after the task. In each case two of the stacked layer's concerns are `unverified` with the packaged head's reason, two stay `qualified`, and the only note is the stacked layer's.". Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_saffron_gates.py::test_the_fast_gates_name_their_tool_and_pass_on_a_clean_tree[lint], and the criterion's witness did not fail.
